content.title: 2026 Boston Marathon winners, records broken, all the details: Recap
content.text: 7:37 pm ET April 20, 2026Best signs and costumes of 2026 Boston Marathon4:40 pm ET April 20, 2026Suni Williams, Zdeno Chára, Chelease Clinton: Celebrities run Boston MarathonThe elite racers in the Boston Marathon are the super stars of their sports, but they aren't necessarily household names. But there were some household names who crossed the finish line.NASA astronaut Sunita “Suni” Williams, a Needham native, who was part of the now-infamous mission was only meant to last a matter of days, but technical issues with the spacecraft left the crew on the orbital outpost for months before they instead returned to Earth on a SpaceX vehicle. She returned from space in March 2025 and retired from NASA in January. She wearing BID ID 608 and finished with a time of 05:52:49.Zdeno Chára, a former Boston Bruins captain, finished his third Boston Marathon race in 03:18:00. He runs for the Thomas E. Smith Foundation.4:28 pm ET April 20, 2026How to qualify for the 2027 Boston MarathonDan SpearsThe Boston Marathon, famously, is one of the toughest long-distance amateur footraces in the world to qualify for.The Boston Athletic Association sets time standards that must be achieved, and even those only to get you into the pool of prospective athletes to run the race. If more people apply to race than there are spots available, those times drop even further.One way that many racers have gotten into the field is to find a marathon with a large downhill elevation change. Races with a net downhill run faster than those on even land, or with more uphills than downhills.Starting with 2027 qualifications, there will be time adjustments made to athletes who submit their finishes from net downhill events.Between 1,500-2,999 feet net downhill results in 5:00 added to finish timeBetween 3,000-5,999 feet net downhill results in 10:00 added to finish timeRaces with more than 6,000 feet of net downhill will no longer be considered for Boston Marathon qualifying.Qualifying race results for the 2027 Boston Marathon started on Sept. 13, 2025. To learn more, go to https://www.baa.org/races/boston-marathon/qualify/Link to 2027 Boston Marathon qualifying times: https://www.baa.org/races/boston-marathon/qualify/2:57 pm ET April 20, 2026Where is the Boston Marathon finish line?Katie LandeckRunners are crossing the Boston Marathon finish line, including former first daughter Chelsea Clinton who was greeted at the finish line by both of her parents.The race ends in Boston's Back Bay, with a stretch down Boylston Street. The finish line is between the Fairfield and Dartmouth Street intersections, near Boston Public Library and Copley Square.1:46 pm ET April 20, 2026Boston Marathon Sensory-Inclusive Viewing ZoneMargie CullenIn a small stretch near mile 13.5 of the Boston Marathon course, there’s a sanctuary from the cowbells and whistles.It’s the second year of the Sensory-Inclusive Viewing Zone, an area equipped with comfortable bean bags chairs, fidget toys, noise cancelling headphones and a ban on cowbells.Laura Amico came up with the idea for a sensory friendly area after she and her family tried to go to the Boston Marathon for the first time three years ago. Her oldest son is on the autism spectrum.“We had a great time, but it was really hard for him with the speakers right next to us and the cowbells and all the sound,”Amico said.She reached out to the BAA about a sensory friendly viewing zone, like there are at other sports events, and “they just ran with it.”“That is amazing, because I love for them to see the athletes doing such incredible work and breaking boundaries,” Amico said. “No matter who you are, no matter what your abilities or disabilities are, it's, I think that's important to see those role models.”1:02 pm ET April 20, 2026Boston Marathon qualifying times for 2027Katie LandeckThinking you want to set a goal to run the Boston Marathon next year? The qualifying period for the 2027 race opened on September 13, 2025. Boston Marathon qualifying times 2027Here are the qualifying times for the 2027 Boston Marathon, which hasn't opened for registration, but you can attempt to achieve qualifying runs for your age group in other qualifying marathons around the world.Age GroupMENWOMENNON-BINARY18-342hrs 55min 00sec3hrs 25min 00sec3hrs 25min 00sec35-393hrs 00min 00sec3hrs 30min 00sec3hrs 30min 00sec40-443hrs 05min 00sec3hrs 35min 00sec3hrs 35min 00sec45-493hrs 15min 00sec3hrs 45min 00sec3hrs 45min 00sec50-543hrs 20min 00sec3hrs 50min 00sec3hrs 50min 00sec55-593hrs 30min 00sec4hrs 00min 00sec4hrs 00min 00sec60-643hrs 50min 00sec4hrs 20min 00sec4hrs 20min 00sec65-694hrs 05min 00sec4hrs 35min 00sec4hrs 35min 00sec70-744hrs 20min 00sec4hrs 50min 00sec4hrs 50min 00sec75-794hrs 35min 00sec5hrs 05min 00sec5hrs 05min 00sec80 and over4hrs 50min 00sec5hrs 20min 00sec5hrs 20min 00secThere is a penalty for net downhill courses. Any course with a net-downhill of 1,500 or more feet will have an index.If the course is net-downhill of between 1,500 and 2,999 feet the runners will have to be five minutes faster than the time above, and if the course is a net-downhill of between 3,000 and 5,999 feet a ten minute time adjustment will be added.12:15 pm ET April 20, 2026New U.S. Women's Boston Marathon record setKatie LandeckBreaking the previous record by more than a minute, Jessica McClain set the new record for an American. She came in fifth place with a time of 2 hours 20 minutes 49 seconds."I'm so honored and privileged to be here," McClain said at the finish line.12:07 pm ET April 20, 2026Sharon Lokedi wins Boston Marathon women's division for second year in a rowKatie LandeckSharon Lokedi, 32, of Kenya broke away at the end to win her second Boston Marathon title and a prize of $150,000.She finished with a time of 2 hours 18 minutes and 51 seconds.She held the lead for the last few miles of the race, creating a clear win for herself. Last year, she was battling it out neck and neck at the finish line.In 2024, she set the course record, finishing with a time of 2:17:22, greeted by her mom as she ran across the finish line. In 2023, she won a silver the Boston Marathon. She's also won the New York Marathon.11:40 am ET April 20, 2026John Korir wins Boston Marathon men's division for second yearKatie LandeckAfter taking a dominating lead midway through the race, John Korir won the title of Boston Marathon champion for the second year in a row. And this time, he clinched the course record, winning him an extra $50,000 in prize money.He finished with a time of 2 hours 1 minute 52 seconds.The course record for the men is Geoffrey Mutai’s record time of 2 hours, 3 minutes and 2 seconds set in 2011.Korir, from Kenya, comes from a running family. His older brother, Wesley Korir, won the Boston Marathon in 2012.Winning the marathon comes with a prize purse of $150,000.11:09 am ET April 20, 2026Chelsea Clinton running Boston Marathon. See celebrities running the raceRin VelascoYes, there are famous people running in today's marathon.Former Boston Bruins player and multi-time Boston Marathon runner Zdeno Chara (Bib Number 3333) is running, and two-time Olympic runner Des Linden (Bib Number 2018) is running as well.The 1968 Boston Marathon winner Amby Burfoot (Bib Number 1968) and former Team USA soccer player Kristine Lilly (Bib Number 1313) are competing in the marathon.Suni Williams (Bib Number 608), the astronaut that was marooned for nine months in space, is running too.From the world of entertainment, Dropkick Murphys musician Jeff DaRosa (Bib Number 29475) is also running in the 130th Boston Marathon. Love Island season 7 winner Bryan Arenales (Bib Number 33689) is participating in this year's race. Comedian Laura Green (Bib Number 1234) is also participating.Chelsea Clinton and former Boston Celtics player Chris Herren are also participating, according to the Boston Athletic Association.10:42 am ET April 20, 2026Women's Wheelchair race winnerKatie LandeckEden Rainbow-Cooper, who won the Boston Marathon women's wheelchair division in 2024, reclaimed her title with another win in 2026. She will take home $15,000 in prize money after taking the lead early in the race.Her time was 1 hours 30 minutes and 51 seconds.Last year, the marathon athlete from the United Kingdom, finished just off the podium.10:32 am ET April 20, 2026Gold-painted wreaths made from olive branchesJoanna K. TzouvelisFour of today's Boston Marathon winners (men’s and women’s open, as well as the men's and women's wheelchair divisions) will be crowned with gold-painted wreaths made from olive branches.They're cut from the historic plains of Marathon, Greece, and they symbolize victory, peace and the enduring ideals of freedom and democracy, Harry Vlachos, president of the Alpha Omega Council, told Wicked Local.While "it all starts here" refers to start of the Boston Marathon in Hopkinton, the start of marathoning as a sport traces back to 19th century Greece. According to the B.A.A., Greece conceived a 40-kilometer (about 24.85 miles) race during the first Olympic games in 1896 that followed the route of the ancient Athenians to remember the Battle of Marathon 2,400 years earlier.George Demeter, the first Greek-American to serve in the Massachusetts House of Representatives, introduced the ancient Greek tradition of crowning marathon winners with laurel wreaths from 1933 to 1945, Vlachos said.10:24 am ET April 20, 2026Marcel Hug wins Boston Marathon men's wheelchair for ninth timeKatie LandeckThe favorite, Marcel Hug of Switzerland, defended his men's wheelchair title, earning his ninth Boston Marathon championship. He finished with a time of 1 hour 16 minutes.Hug previously won the title in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2021, 2023 and 2024, 2025. He is also the reigning course record holder with a 1:15:33 finish in 2024, which broke the previous course record he set in 2023.10:22 am ET April 20, 2026What time does the Boston Marathon end?Katie LandeckThat depends on exactly what you're asking.The finish line closes 5:30 p.m., according to the Boston Athletic Association. However, not every runner will have crossed the finish line at that point. Runners still on the course are asked to move to the sidewalk to finish. Roads are typically reopening along the route as the majority of the runners pass through.But if what you're asking it when to the elite runners finish, that's much earlier. For the elite runners, which have staggered start times, the men typically finish around 11:45 and the women around 12:10.10:10 am ET April 20, 2026Zdeno Chara running third Boston MarathonCait KempBoston Bruins legend Zdeno Chara is running the Boston Marathon for the third time. The 2011 Stanley Cup champion previously ran in 2023 and 2024. In 2024, he finished in 3:30:52 and in 3:38:23 in 2023. Chara won't be hard to spot on the course as he stands at 6-9. Chara served as the starter for the men's professional wave. 10:08 am ET April 20, 2026How long is the Boston Marathon?Katie LandeckThe Boston Marathon is the standard marathon length of 26.2 miles.The marathon traces its roots to ancient Greece. According to legend, Pheidippides ran from the plains of Marathon to Athens to deliver the news that the Greek Army had won a crucial battle against the invading Persian Army.“Rejoice, we are victorious,” he announced before falling dead. While his run was only 24.8 miles, it became the story behind the modern Olympic Marathon. The marathon distance was lengthened to 26.2 miles to suit the wishes of the British royal family in the 1908 Olympic Games and this distance became the Olympic standard in 1924.Where does Boston Marathon end?The race ends in Boston's Back Bay, with a stretch down Boylston Street. The finish line is between the Fairfield and Dartmouth Street intersections, near Boston Public Library and Copley Square.10:00 am ET April 20, 2026Boston Marathon Announcer: Who is Hannah StormRin VelascoSportsCenter anchor Hannah Storm is announcing the 130th Boston Marathon on the national broadcast.With over 40 years of reporting experience, Storm is an accomplished sports journalist currently working for ESPN.She is married to Dan Hicks, the lead golf play-by-play commentator for NBC Sports.She is announcing today's race with running commentator John Anderson.(A previous version of this post had the wrong person commentating with Hannah Storm. This has been updated with the correct information.)9:50 am ET April 20, 2026'He's been putting in a lot of time and effort'Caroline BunnellWith the wheelchair races for both men and women underway, spectators have packed the sidewalks in Hopkinton. Sophie and Aiden Thomas, of Millbury, were up along the fence to get a front row seat to watch their father, Paul, compete in the men's wheelchair race for the fifth time. "We're proud of him," Aiden Thomas said. "He's been putting in a lot of time and effort.""It's been fun to watch him get ready and train," Sophie Thomas said.9:47 am ET April 20, 2026Professional Women start timeRin VelascoThe Professional Women's racers are off. The course record to beat is 2 hours 17 minutes 22 seconds, set by Kenya's Sharon Lokedi in 2025.9:38 am ET April 20, 2026Professional Men start timeRin VelascoThe Professional Men's race are off for the Boston Marathon.The course record for the men is Geoffrey Mutai’s record time of 2 hours, 3 minutes and 2 seconds set in 2011.9:35 am ET April 20, 2026'Hope to enjoy the day, run sub-2:50'Caroline BunnellEtienne Dubois, of Quebec, said he's feeling prepared as he heads into his first Boston Marathon; he qualified after racing in Montreal. Dubois starts at 10 a.m. in the first wave of Corral 1. He said he arrived two days ago and has enjoyed getting the full experience of all the Marathon has to offer."The organization has been amazing, and I'm looking forward to the start," Dubois said. "I just hope to enjoy the day but I'm aiming for sub-2:50 today."Franklin resident Kevin Tucceri, who's running for the 14th straight year, said he can't wait to feel the energy from the crowd again. "Boston is so special, it's the grand of all," Tucceri said. "The other thing is the spectators, the volunteers. I don't think there's a more well run, organized marathon in the world than Boston."And while temperatures seem chilly for spectators, runners say mid-40s is perfect with the sun shining and a slight breeze. Tucceri said he remembers running in 2012 when it got over 80, and another year when it was in the 30s and snowing and runners had to drop out due to hypothermia."The weather seems to be perfect," Tucceri said. I think it's ideal conditions."9:34 am ET April 20, 2026Handcycle and Duo start timeRin VelascoThe Handcycle and Duo participants' are off in the Boston Marathon.Next to start will be the professional men at 9:37 a.m. ET.9:22 am ET April 20, 2026What is the prize money for the Boston Marathon?Katie LandeckRecognition isn’t the only thing athletes compete for; there’s the prize money after all. In fact, there's a guarantee purse of $1.13 million this year that could go up to $1.33 million.The Boston Marathon is offering five- to six-figure rewards for the top finishers in the competition, with a $50,000 bonus for those who set new course records in the open division and wheelchair division. In the open division, the first-place prize is $150,000, the second-place prize is $75,000 and the third-place runner receives $40,000. There is prize money down to $5,500 for 10th place.In the wheelchair division for T53/54/34 competitors, the first-, second-, and third-place prizes are valued at $50,000, $30,000 and $15,000. There is prize money down to $1,500 for 10th place.To get the $50,000 course record bonus, open division male runners will have to beat Geoffrey Mutai’s record time of 2 hours, 3 minutes and 2 seconds set in 2011.Open division female runners will have to beat 2 hours 17 minutes 22 seconds, set by Kenya's Sharon Lokedi in 2025.Male wheelchair athletes will have to beat Marcel Hug’s record of 1 hour, 15 minutes and 33 seconds in 2024, while female wheelchair athletes must beat Manuela Schär’s 1 hour, 28 minutes and 17 seconds in 2017 to get the bonus. 9:12 am ET April 20, 2026Boston Marathon wheelchair times: How fast they goKatie LandeckEvery year, wheelchair athletes are some of the fiercest competitors participating in the Boston Marathon. This year is no different. The current high-performance standard for male wheelchair athletes is less than 1 hour and 31 minutes. For female wheelchair athletes, it’s less than 1 hour and 52 minutes. 9:07 am ET April 20, 2026Boston Marathon startsRin VelascoThe Men's Wheelchair race started at 9:06 a.m. Eastern Time, kicking off the Boston Marathon.Reminder these are the start times for the other races:Men’s Wheelchair 9:06 a.m. ETWomen’s Wheelchair 9:09 a.m. ETHandcycle & Duo Participants 9:30 a.m. ETProfessional Men 9:37 a.m. ETProfessional Women 9:47 a.m. ETPara Athletics Divisions 9:50 a.m. ETWave 1 10 a.m. ETWave 2 10:25 a.m. ETWave 3 10:50 a.m. ETWave 4 11:15 a.m. ET8:56 am ET April 20, 2026Born in Framingham, cheering from Mile 6!Dan O'BrienMarathon Monday excitement was underway last Friday, April 17, at Framingham Union Hospital, where the newest members of the community are adding a burst of baby-sized spirit to the race-day tradition.According to a press release from the hospital, babies born in Framingham Union's Beautiful Beginnings Birth Center were dressed in Marathon‑themed outfits, complete with tiny sneaker socks and medals, to honor the Marathon as it runs through Framingham at Mile 6. The youngsters sported race numbers that represented the time they were born, and they even had bottles ready for milk stops and hydration stations, according to the hospital. 8:31 am ET April 20, 2026Runners arrive at the starting line, take in the sceneryCaroline BunnellAthletes began arriving at the starting line area around 7:30. Many took in their surroundings, taking out their phones to capture their arrival at the iconic course as they got off buses at the staging area. More spectators have arrived, as the race gets underway in less than an hour. Alan Mendez said he was excited to watch the race for the first time and is especially interested in seeing how the runners prepare to start the race."I'm excited to see how the racers get ready and prep, before they start heading out," Mendez said. "Obviously, everyone wants to see how they finish but I think to see how excited they will be at the very beginning is a very important part."7:44 am ET April 20, 2026Boston weather forecast for Marathon MondayRin VelascoGood news, marathon runners: It's not going to be hot.National Weather Service meteorologist Caitlyn Mensch said to expect morning temperatures in the mid-to-upper 30s that are set to climb to an noon or early afternoon high of low 50s which are set to come back down to low 40s in the afternoon.Morning runners should see "pretty clear skies" in the morning, which are not ideal for marathon runners, but Mensch said that as the afternoon hours approach, more clouds should come in, with afternoon skies being "decently overcast."There may be isolated showers during the afternoon, and wind gusts should blowing between six to 12 miles per hour.7:32 am ET April 20, 2026Northbridge family is stoked to cheer first-time qualifierCaroline BunnellAs temperatures hover just above freezing at the Boston Marathon starting line in Hopkinton, volunteers are getting the final touches in place in time for the race. Barriers are being pulled into place, and spectators are beginning to claim their spots.Sarah Talbot, of Northbridge, grabbed a muffin from the Muffin House Cafe tent set up near the starting line. She's waiting to cheer on her older sister, who is running the Marathon for the first time after qualifying.This is also Talbot's first time attending the race, and she's excited for the energy the event brings to the area."I'm excited about the hype that it brings to Hopkinton," she said. "I'm one of five siblings, so we are all posted up along the whole race to support our sister."7:02 am ET April 20, 2026How do you qualify for the Boston Marathon?Katie LandeckThe Boston Marathon is a hard race to qualify for, and it keeps getting tougher. This crop of runners is the fastest to ever qualify."This year’s ‘Cut-Off’ time needed to gain acceptance into the Boston Marathon was four minutes, thirty-four seconds or faster (4:34) than the qualifying time for each respective age group and gender," the association said.Age GroupMENWOMENNON-BINARY18-342hrs 55min 00sec3hrs 25min 00sec3hrs 25min 00sec35-393hrs 00min 00sec3hrs 30min 00sec3hrs 30min 00sec40-443hrs 05min 00sec3hrs 35min 00sec3hrs 35min 00sec45-493hrs 15min 00sec3hrs 45min 00sec3hrs 45min 00sec50-543hrs 20min 00sec3hrs 50min 00sec3hrs 50min 00sec55-593hrs 30min 00sec4hrs 00min 00sec4hrs 00min 00sec60-643hrs 50min 00sec4hrs 20min 00sec4hrs 20min 00sec65-694hrs 05min 00sec4hrs 35min 00sec4hrs 35min 00sec70-744hrs 20min 00sec4hrs 50min 00sec4hrs 50min 00sec75-794hrs 35min 00sec5hrs 05min 00sec5hrs 05min 00sec80 and over4hrs 50min 00sec5hrs 20min 00sec5hrs 20min 00sec6:00 am ET April 20, 2026Where to watch the Boston MarathonMargie Cullen and Rin VelascoIf you are rooting for someone who is running in the marathon and want to see them pass by, there are a eight spots that are considered prime to watch from.The Boston Athletic Association spectator's guide available guide suggests picks these spots:Hopkinton's Main Street at the start of the marathon (0 miles to 1.90 miles)Ashland station (1.90 miles to 4.95 miles)Framingham Train Depot (4.95 miles to 7.52 miles)Natick Common on Center Street (7.52 miles to 11.72 miles)Near the Wellesley Scream Tunnel (11.72 miles to 15.93 miles)Newton Hills (15.93 miles to 21.35 miles)Beacon Street in Brookline (22.45 miles to 24.70 miles)Boylston Street in Boston. (21.35 miles to 22.45 miles or 24.70 to Finish Line)Make sure to check the spectator's guide to see what time which racers will be passing through.5:35 am ET April 20, 2026'Just wait until you experience the Marathon'Dan O'BrienThe motto in Hopkinton is "It All Starts Here." And just as runners from throughout the world train for months to ensure peak performance on Patriots' Day, so too does this community of nearly 20,000 residents, building upon generations of civic pride to provide their guests "a single, unforgettable moment at the start line," according to a press release from the aptly named Hopkinton Marathon Committee.The Committee, whose mission is to guide and help coordinate all Boston Athletic Association (B.A.A.) efforts within Hopkinton, recently announced that spectators at the start line will be treated to a select group of local public servants to serve as starters for Waves 3-6. It's an honor that the B.A.A. has extended to the Committee for 20 years.Here are the 2026 starters, all of whom represent decades of service and dedication to Hopkinton:Fire Chief and Emergency Management Director Gary Daugherty (Wave 3);Recently retired Water-Sewer Manager Eric Carty (Wave 4);Recently retired Superintendent of Schools Carol Cavanaugh (Wave 5);The family of the late Henry Arthur “Artie” Pyne, who served Hopkinton as a volunteer firefighter and special police detail officer for 45 years (Wave 6)“Just wait until you experience the Marathon,” Cavanaugh recalls being told shortly after arriving in Hopkinton eight years ago, per the Hopkinton Marathon Committee's release.As for the 130th edition of the Marathon, the wait is over.5:30 am ET April 20, 2026What is the Boston Marathon route?Margie Cullen and Rin VelascoThe Boston Marathon starts on Main Street in Hopkinton. Runners will then follow Route 135 through Ashland, Framingham, Natick and Wellesley to where Route 135 turns into Route 16.The course goes along Route 16 until the fire station at Commonwealth Avenue, where runners will take a right and begin the stretch of Newton Hills. After Heartbreak Hill from mile 20 to 21, runners will pass the Chestnut Hill Reservoir before turning left on to Beacon Street.At this point, runners will have just about four miles to go. They will continue through Brookline, Kenmore Square, and under Massachusetts Avenue.Finally, the famous turns come at the end: right onto Hereford Street and left onto Boylston Street for the final sprint.The Marathon ends near the Boston Public Library in Copley Square.You can see a map of the course here.5:16 am ET April 20, 2026What are the Boston Marathon Road closures?Katie LandeckThe Boston Athletic Association provided this chart for the marathon course road closures looking generally at timing.LOCATIONTIME OF CLOSUREHopkinton7:15 a.m. - 1:30 p.m.Ashland7:15 a.m. - 1:20 p.m.Framingham7:30 a.m. - 1:55 p.m.Natick8:30 a.m. - 2:45 p.m.Wellesley8:30 a.m. - 3:35 p.m.Newton8:00 a.m. - 4:45 p.m.Brookline9:00 a.m. - 5:45 p.m.BostonVariable - 7:00 p.m.But it you want specifics, here's a town by town breakdown.HopkintonHopkinton will close immediately surrounding the start line and town common (Main Street, Ash Street, Park Street, and Hayden Rowe) at 6:30 a.m. Other roads leading to the downtown closed at 7 a.m.They included.West Main Street at Lumber StreetWood Street at Elm StreetHayden Rowe Street at ChestnutAsh Street at Blueberry LaneCedar Street at Legacy Farms NorthEast Main Street at every intersectionThe town will also block roadways adjacent to where runners, spectators, volunteers and workers will be.AshlandAshland Police Department will close Route 135 at 7:15 a.m. until the runners were through. The closure typically lasts through early afternoon.FraminghamIn Framingham, Waverly Street/Route 135 will close from 8:45 a.m. to 2 p.m.NatickIn Natick, Route 135 will close from about 8:30 to 3 p.m., according to the town.WellesleyRoads in Wellesley will close at 8:30 a.m. and remained closed through the end of the race, at about 3:30 p.m.5:08 am ET April 20, 2026How to track Boston Marathon runnersKatie LandeckIs there someone you want to track as they race today? There's an app for that.The BAA Racing App is available in both the Apple and Android store, which will allow you to track runners.If apps aren't your thing, BAA website has live tracking. If you have a runner's bib number or name you can follow their race and see the results at the finish line.4:46 am ET April 20, 2026What time does the Boston Marathon start?Katie LandeckPeople start arriving for the Boston Marathon early in the morning, but the times the actual races start varies.These are the start times for athletes competing in the day's races, according to the Athletic Association:Men’s Wheelchair 9:06 a.m. ETWomen’s Wheelchair 9:09 a.m. ETHandcycle & Duo Participants 9:30 a.m. ETProfessional Men 9:37 a.m. ETProfessional Women 9:47 a.m. ETPara Athletics Divisions 9:50 a.m. ETWave 1 10 a.m. ETWave 2 10:25 a.m. ETWave 3 10:50 a.m. ETWave 4 11:15 a.m. ET4:00 am ET April 20, 2026How to watch, live stream the Boston marathonKatie LandeckWCVB Channel 5 (ABC) will be covering the Boston Marathon live for all Boston-area viewers beginning at 4 a.m. on Marathon Monday.It will be simulcast regionally on its sister stations: WMUR News 9 ABC (Manchester, NH), WMTW Channel 8 ABC (Portland/Auburn, ME), and WPTZ NBC5 (Burlington, VT/Plattsburgh, NY).Local viewers can also live stream the marathon on the Very Local app.How to watch the Boston Marathon: NationalESPN2 will provide live national coverage of the Boston Marathon from 9 a.m. ET until 12:30 p.m. ET, as well as some other coverage on other ESPN shows and platforms before and after that time. The marathon will be streamed on ESPN+.Watch it on ESPN+!How to watch the Boston Marathon: InternationalHere are some stations that will be broadcasting the race internationally:Olympic ChannelFloSportsTSN/RDSSMGESPN BrazilESPN LATAM/SurEurosport IndiaEurosportVTVCabSupersportIf you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission.
